title: NPS / RADIUS Authentication Monitoring
exclusions: Detects locally defined concentrations of Windows NPS Security event 6273 reason code 16 (Microsoft documents this as incorrect-password authentication failure): at least 10 failures in one complete five-minute bucket from the same NPS server, NAS, and calling-station identifier, classified as single-account guessing when one account is present or multi-account spraying when five or more distinct accounts are present. It does not label 6273 reasons other than 16, event 6274 discarded requests, 6279 NPS lockout, RADIUS protocol errors, unknown clients, invalid message authenticators, accounting failures, Access-Accept, session state, MFA extension behavior, certificate/EAP negotiation, network policy mismatch, or NPS availability as credential attacks. Calling-Station-ID is NAS-supplied and may be absent, transformed, shared, spoofed, or a MAC/device identifier; it is not proof of a person or source IP. The thresholds, bucket, ten-minute delay, identity coalesces, severities, and exception contract are local policy, not Microsoft, Splunk, or MITRE defaults. Missing NPS hosts/events/fields, disabled audit policy, Security-log overwrite, collection lag, and duplicated routes are source-health failures rather than successful authentication. This UC performs no account, NPS, NAS, network, MFA, password, certificate, or policy action and makes no compliance claim.
evidence: After deployment, retain the authoritative NPS/NAS/policy inventory; effective `Audit Network Policy Server` Success/Failure policy; Security-log retention and XML input/add-on configuration; representative raw 6272/6273 events and reason-code fields; independent host/source/extraction health; version-controlled `windows_nps_reason16_failure_concentration` saved search, ACL, schedule, dispatch history, and result rows; dashboard/alert revisions; privacy/access design for account and station identifiers; NAS/VPN/WLAN and identity correlation; bounded exceptions; incident disposition; and dated positive, negative, threshold, distinct-account, identity, duplicate, delayed, and malformed-event tests. Preserve NPS server, NAS, calling/called station, account set, reason, policy/authentication fields, counts, bucket, record IDs, and event/index times. This documentation-only review created no NPS, RADIUS, Windows, Splunk, alert, dashboard, account, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index and fixed complete five-minute bucket, ingest exactly 10 XML Security events 6273 from `Computer=nps01.example`, `NASIPv4Address=192.0.2.10`, `CallingStationID=00-11-22-33-44-55`, and `ReasonCode=16`, each with a distinct EventRecordID. Use one `User_Account_Name` in the first fixture and expect one `single_account_guessing` result with `reason16_failures=10` and `distinct_accounts=1`. Repeat with ten events distributed evenly across five accounts and expect one `multi_account_spraying` row with `distinct_accounts=5`; equality at both thresholds must alert.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run isolated variants and expect zero rows: nine reason-16 failures for one account; ten reason-16 failures across two, three, or four accounts (an intentionally unclassified middle case); any count of 6273 with reason other than 16; 6272 success, 6274 discard, or 6279 lockout events; mixed NAS/calling-station/NPS identities that do not independently reach threshold; missing or dash-only user, NAS, calling station, reason, server, or record identity; wrong provider/source/type; duplicate replay of one record; and events outside the closed bucket. The source-health/operational views must still surface malformed data, 6274/6279, unknown clients, audit gaps, and unclassified denial spikes rather than interpreting zero primary rows as healthy.

dataSources: Primary source is XML-rendered Windows Security events on every NPS server: `index=wineventlog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, provider `Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing`. Microsoft documents 6272 grant, 6273 deny, 6274 discard, and other NPS states under Audit Network Policy Server; this detector requires 6273 plus numeric Reason Code 16. Required extracted identities are NPS server (`dest`, `Computer`, or `host`), user (`User_Account_Name`, `UserName`, or `Account_Name`), NAS IPv4/IPv6/identifier, Calling Station Identifier, and EventRecordID. Preserve Called Station, RADIUS client name/IP, connection-request/network policy, authentication provider/server/type, EAP type, account session ID, reason text, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Supporting sources include NPS text/SQL accounting, NAS/VPN/WLAN/controller logs, AD/Entra MFA, certificate/EAP, firewall, and asset/identity data.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) for Security event collection, extraction, and Authentication-model mappings for NPS events. A local security app owns saved search `windows_nps_reason16_failure_concentration`, NPS source-health and operational searches, dashboard, tests, privacy controls, bounded exceptions, and alert routing. Splunk Enterprise Security is optional.
spl:
index=wineventlog source="XmlWinEventLog:Security" sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" EventCode=6273 earliest=-15m@m latest=-10m@m
| eval provider=coalesce(Provider_Name,ProviderName,SourceName), nps_server=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(dest),""),nullif(trim(Computer),""),nullif(trim(ComputerName),""),nullif(trim(host),""))), account=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(User_Account_Name),""),nullif(trim(UserName),""),nullif(trim(Account_Name),""))), calling_station=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(Calling_Station_Identifier),""),nullif(trim(CallingStationID),""))), nas=lower(coalesce(nullif(trim(NAS_IPv4_Address),""),nullif(trim(NASIPAddress),""),nullif(trim(NAS_IPv6_Address),""),nullif(trim(NAS_Identifier),""))), reason_code=tonumber(coalesce(Reason_Code,ReasonCode)), event_record_id=trim(tostring(coalesce(EventRecordID,RecordNumber)))
| where provider="Microsoft-Windows-Security-Auditing" AND len(nps_server)>0 AND len(account)>0 AND account!="-" AND len(calling_station)>0 AND calling_station!="-" AND len(nas)>0 AND nas!="-" AND reason_code=16 AND len(event_record_id)>0
| eval event_identity=nps_server."|".source."|".event_record_id
| dedup event_identity
| bin _time span=5m
| stats count as reason16_failures dc(account) as distinct_accounts values(account) as accounts values(event_record_id) as event_record_ids values(Connection_Request_Policy_Name) as connection_request_policies values(Network_Policy_Name) as network_policies values(Authentication_Type) as authentication_types values(EAP_Type) as eap_types min(_indextime) as first_index_time max(_indextime) as last_index_time by _time nps_server nas calling_station
| eval signal=case(reason16_failures>=10 AND distinct_accounts=1,"single_account_guessing",reason16_failures>=10 AND distinct_accounts>=5,"multi_account_spraying")
| where isnotnull(signal)
| eval local_severity=if(signal="multi_account_spraying","high","medium"), reason_code=16, failure_threshold=10, spray_account_threshold=5, use_case="UC-1.2.98", bucket_start=strftime(_time,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
| table _time nps_server nas calling_station signal local_severity reason_code reason16_failures distinct_accounts accounts connection_request_policies network_policies authentication_types eap_types event_record_ids first_index_time last_index_time failure_threshold spray_account_threshold bucket_start use_case
| sort 0 -reason16_failures -distinct_accounts nps_server nas calling_station
description: Detects concentrated NPS incorrect-password denials using Microsoft Security event 6273 reason code 16. Within each complete five-minute bucket it identifies at least ten failures from one NPS/NAS/calling-station identity, classifying one targeted account as repeated guessing and five or more accounts as spray-like behavior while preserving exact policy, protocol, account-set, record, and timing context.
value: VPN, wireless, wired 802.1X, and other RADIUS-backed access can fail because of users, devices, certificates, policies, shared infrastructure, or attacks. Restricting this security analytic to Microsoft's documented incorrect-password reason and transparent per-station thresholds gives responders actionable concentration evidence, while separate operational views preserve all grants, denials, discards, lockouts, and source gaps so ordinary NPS faults are not mislabeled as credential attacks.
implementation: Enable Success and Failure for the Windows `Audit Network Policy Server` subcategory on every governed NPS server, collect the Security channel as XML with `Splunk_TA_windows`, and validate actual 6272/6273/6274 fields and volume. Save the primary SPL as `windows_nps_reason16_failure_concentration`; run every five minutes over a closed bucket delayed ten minutes. Treat ten failures, one-account, and five-account cutoffs as local starting policy and maintain separate source-health and all-result operational searches. Correlate alerts with NPS reason/policy/EAP fields, NAS/controller/VPN logs, identity state, MFA/certificate, asset ownership, and approved tests before response.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows NPS — Authentication and Source Health`: show expected NPS/audit-policy coverage, newest Security event age, malformed fields, Security-log overwrite/lag, duplicate routes, and NAS inventory first. Show 6272/6273/6274/6279 trends and reason-code distribution as operational context, then primary single-account and multi-account findings. Include NPS, NAS, calling/called station, account set/count, reason, request/network policy, authentication/EAP type, record IDs, bucket, delay, owner, exception, and disposition. Drill down to raw Security XML, Event Viewer custom NPS view, NAS/VPN/WLAN logs, accounting session, identity/lockout/MFA/certificate, network telemetry, and change. Protect user/device identifiers and never render missing data as success.
schema: Raw XML Windows NPS Security events with reason-code and NAS/calling-station identity contract
dataModelAcceleration: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows maps Windows event data, including NPS 6272/6273, into Authentication-related knowledge. A generic accelerated `action=failure` search is not equivalent to this detector because it need not preserve NPS Reason Code 16, Calling Station Identifier, NAS identity, request/network policy, EAP type, EventRecordID, or source-health state. Use raw events for the primary contract; a purpose-built summary may be used only after parity tests preserve all dimensions, event identity, bucket, and late/duplicate handling.

knownFalsePositives:
A returned row is a real concentration of reason-16 denials under the local identity/threshold contract, not proof of hostile guessing.

1. **User repeatedly enters an old or wrong password** — Cached credentials on a phone, laptop, VPN client, mapped service, or supplicant can retry one account. Confirm owner, station identity, recent password change, account state, client logs, and whether attempts stop after supported remediation. Do not reset or disable automatically.

2. **Shared device or identity configuration** — Kiosks, conference devices, scanners, phones, machine authentication, and MAC-auth bypass can present shared or device-derived identifiers. Determine whether `account` is human, computer, device, or MAC and whether Calling-Station-ID is stable for that NAS.

3. **NAS/controller retry behavior** — Wireless controllers, switches, VPN gateways, proxies, and RADIUS clients can retransmit or retry one failed exchange. Correlate NAS request IDs/session identifiers and vendor logs; ten Windows events need not equal ten human password entries.

4. **Password rotation or deployment drift** — A service/device secret or user password can change while stored credentials remain stale across many devices, producing spray-like multi-account patterns behind one controller. Check change timing, MDM/GPO/VPN profile rollout, policy, and site impact before escalating as attack.

5. **Approved penetration test or authentication load test** — Require exact calling station/NAS, accounts, test ID, owner, approver, start, exclusive expiry, and rollback. Use test accounts and isolated paths; never lock real users merely to validate the alert.

6. **Identifier aggregation behind infrastructure** — Calling-Station-ID can be blank, reused, normalized, or represent a shared proxy/controller depending on NAS. The primary search excludes missing values but cannot prove endpoint identity. Use NAS logs and session/called-station context.

7. **NPS or directory fault presented as reason 16** — Microsoft directs operators to check credentials, account lock, correct domain controller, and account existence. A directory targeting, replication, or policy issue can affect many users. Correlate DC/NPS health and do not assume password spray solely from account breadth.

8. **Replay/duplicate collection** — WEF plus direct forwarding, checkpoint reset, or restored Security logs can repeat one EventRecordID. The search deduplicates in-window, while source health must preserve and correct the route.

**Safe notification suppression:** apply after the base result using exact `nps_server,nas,calling_station,signal` and, for single-account cases, exact account, with numeric inclusive start, exclusive expiry, owner, approver, ticket, test/change ID, and reason. Reject wildcards, permanent NAS/controller exceptions, broad site/account ranges, and suppression of audit/source/extraction failures.
hardware: Windows Server systems running Network Policy Server for RADIUS-backed VPN, wireless, wired 802.1X, or other governed access. Non-Windows RADIUS, cloud authentication proxies, managed NAC, Entra MFA extension-only logs, and NAS/controller telemetry require separate source and field contracts.
reviewer: documentation-only editorial review against primary Microsoft Audit Network Policy Server event inventory, current NPS troubleshooting/reason-code guidance, and NPS accounting/planning documentation plus Splunk Microsoft Windows add-on source/CIM mapping documentation; audit policy, event fields, NAS/calling-station semantics, SPL, thresholds, fixtures, source health, privacy, dashboard, alerting, and production response were specified but not executed or Microsoft/Splunk/NPS/RADIUS/NAS/identity/security-operations SME signed

cost.search_load_notes: The primary search reads one Security event ID over a closed five-minute bucket and performs bounded deduplication and cardinality aggregation. NPS Security events can be medium/high volume; broader 6272/6274/6279 operational dashboards and accounting retention add separate ingest/search cost.
sources: optional NPS RADIUS accounting and NAS logs

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and signal contract

Assign NPS/RADIUS, network/NAS, identity, VPN/wireless, Windows logging, Splunk detection, privacy, and incident owners. Inventory every active NPS server and proxy, RADIUS client/NAS, friendly name/IP, site, access service, connection-request/network policy, authentication method/EAP type, certificate/MFA extension, remote RADIUS group, accounting destination, and service owner. Keep an expected server/NAS inventory outside event data so an omitted NPS is not mistaken for quiet authentication.

Microsoft's Audit Network Policy Server subcategory covers Grant, Deny, Discard, Quarantine, Lock, and Unlock. The primary detector uses only Security event 6273 and only numeric Reason Code 16, which Microsoft's current troubleshooting guidance describes as authentication failure because the user's password is incorrect, while directing operators to check credentials, account lock, correct domain controller, and account existence. Other reasons often represent policy, certificate, EAP, directory, or configuration conditions and must remain visible in operational dashboards but are not silently called password guessing.

Define one event as one accepted unique NPS Security record, not one human keystroke or one RADIUS packet. The NAS can retry; Calling-Station-ID is supplied by network access infrastructure and can represent a MAC/device, proxy, or shared value. The local starting rule groups by NPS server, NAS, calling station, and complete five-minute bucket. Ten reason-16 denials to exactly one account becomes `single_account_guessing`; ten denials across at least five accounts becomes `multi_account_spraying`. Two through four accounts are intentionally unclassified for the primary alert but remain in operations. Equality at 10 and 5 alerts. These are transparent local thresholds, not vendor constants.

Plan privacy and authorization. Account, station, NAS, session, and policy fields can identify people/devices and access patterns. Limit raw/dashboard/export access; hash or tokenize broad reporting only if analysts retain an approved reversible or drilldown path for incident response. The search role needs Security-index read and scheduling rights; alert actions need no account disable/reset, NAS block, NPS-policy write, certificate, MFA, or network-control rights.

## Step 1 — Enable and verify Windows NPS auditing

On every governed NPS, verify effective audit state under policy management and locally:

```cmd
auditpol /get /subcategory:"Network Policy Server"
```

Microsoft's troubleshooting guidance provides this command and the enablement form:

```cmd
auditpol /set /subcategory:"Network Policy Server" /success:enable /failure:enable
```

Use centrally reviewed policy rather than unmanaged local drift. Success events are needed for denominator and service validation even though the primary search uses failures. Record effective policy, GPO precedence, NPS role/state, Security log maximum/retention settings, and change. Monitor audit-policy change separately. A configured default on one Windows release is not evidence that every server retains it.

Install a supported Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows and collect `[WinEventLog://Security]` with XML rendering through an app-owned stanza. Validate local event generation in Event Viewer **Custom Views > Server Roles > Network Policy and Access Services** and compare exact EventRecordID with Splunk. Confirm `source=XmlWinEventLog:Security`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, provider, EventCode, Computer/dest, account, Calling/Called Station Identifier, NAS IPv4/IPv6/Identifier, RADIUS client, request/network policy, authentication provider/server/type, EAP type, session ID, Reason Code/text, `_time`, and `_indextime`. Field spellings can vary by add-on/event rendering; qualify each coalesce against raw XML.

Maintain source health that reports expected NPS missing, effective audit policy not Success/Failure, stale 6272/6273/6274/canary, Security-log overwrite pressure, forwarding backlog, malformed required fields, provider/source drift, duplicate EventRecordID route, future event, excessive delay, and sudden per-NAS volume collapse. No failures can be normal; use a safe test account/path or event/configuration inventory to prove collection. Never generate repeated production failures that could lock an account merely to test monitoring.

## Step 2 — Configure supporting accounting and NAS evidence

Microsoft documents NPS accounting to text, SQL, or parallel destinations for authentication/accounting requests and sessions. Decide whether session investigations require it and configure through NPS Accounting with capacity, retention, database availability, credential, encryption, and failover review. Accounting is supporting evidence, not a substitute for Security reason codes in this detector. Monitor logging failures so an unavailable text path or SQL `report_event` destination is not invisible.

Collect the corresponding VPN gateway, wireless controller/AP, switch, NAC, firewall, and remote RADIUS proxy logs with stable NAS/client/session identifiers. Preserve RADIUS Access-Request/Accept/Reject, retry/request authenticator where available, station and called station, assigned address, port/type, and session timing. NPS event counts can exceed user interactions due to retries; NAS evidence explains that multiplier.

For EAP/TLS and Microsoft Entra MFA extension paths, collect certificate-chain/expiry/trust, client supplicant, AzureMfa AuthN/AuthZ, and extension health under separate access controls. Do not interpret every reason-16 cluster as an MFA or certificate problem. Maintain DC/domain/DNS/time/replication health and account state to investigate Microsoft's listed alternatives.

## Step 3 — Create and understand the primary SPL

Save sidecar `spl` verbatim as `windows_nps_reason16_failure_concentration`. Schedule every five minutes with a ten-minute delay. At 12:15, `earliest=-15m@m latest=-10m@m` covers 12:00 through but not including 12:05. Measure p99 Security-event indexing delay; move both bounds together while keeping closed nonoverlap and add late-event reconciliation if necessary.

The base search fixes XML Security, provider, Event 6273, and one five-minute horizon. `eval` normalizes NPS server, account, calling station, NAS, numeric reason, and record identity. Required blank/dash identities are rejected from trusted attribution and must appear in source health. Reason must equal 16 exactly. Event identity combines NPS, source, and record ID; dedup protects result count from replay but does not absolve duplicate routing.

After `bin`, `stats` counts records and distinct accounts by exact NPS/NAS/calling station. It preserves account set, record IDs, policy/authentication fields, and index-time range. The classification has an intentional gap: one account or five-plus accounts can alert at ten-plus failures, while two-to-four accounts produce no primary row. This avoids arbitrarily calling a small shared-device pattern either brute force or spray. Track the gap in an operational view and tune only with measured baseline, service risk, retry behavior, and review.

Do not replace this with a generic `tstats action=failure` threshold. Authentication CIM can support cross-source analytics, but this rule depends on NPS Reason Code 16 and exact NAS/calling-station identity. Generic `src` may mean NAS rather than endpoint, and the accelerated event may omit reason, policy, EAP, and record identity. Document any CIM derivative as separate behavior.

## Step 4 — Validate threshold, identity, and NPS behavior

Use the exact fixed-time fixtures in `controlTest`. Assert exact bucket start, NPS/NAS/station, count, distinct accounts, account values, branch, thresholds, record IDs, policy/protocol values, and index-time range. Test 9/10/11 failures; 1/4/5/6 accounts; repeated and distinct record IDs; same station across two NASs; same NAS across NPSs; case normalization; dash/missing fields; IPv4/IPv6/NAS identifier fallbacks; nonnumeric reason; wrong provider/channel; bucket edges; late indexing; and search rerun.

In a nonproduction NPS/NAS environment, create test accounts that cannot affect real access. Generate a small number of ordinary accept/deny/discard cases and compare Event Viewer, Splunk, NPS policy, NAS logs, and optional accounting by session/request. For threshold tests, replay sanitized XML or use an isolated access lab with lockout policy understood and approved. Never send ten bad passwords to a production or privileged account, weaken lockout/MFA/EAP, expose a RADIUS shared secret, or use real employee/device identifiers in fixtures.

Validate reason 16 against the exact Windows build and current Microsoft guidance. Exercise other reasons (policy mismatch, certificate/EAP, disabled/expired/locked account where safe) only to prove they do not enter this primary detector and remain visible operationally. Test NAS retransmission so responders understand events-per-user-action.

Measure Security event rate, log wrap, forwarder/index lag, ingest bytes, search runtime, scheduler skips, cardinality/multivalue size, alert rate, and privacy export. Keep `status=draft` until NPS, network, identity, Splunk, privacy, and SOC owners accept collection, identities, thresholds, fixtures, source health, dashboard, delivery, exceptions, and response.

## Step 5 — Operationalize triage and response

Alert title should state `Concentrated NPS incorrect-password denials` with the branch, never `account compromised`. Include NPS, NAS, calling station, accounts/counts, exact reason, request/network policies, authentication/EAP type, five-minute UTC bucket, delay/source health, station/NAS owner, exception, and runbook.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify raw 6273 records, provider/source, reason 16, EventRecordIDs, exact identities, bucket/count/cardinality, delay, duplicates, and audit/source health.
2. Determine what Calling-Station-ID means for this NAS and map it through authoritative controller/NAC/asset inventory; do not assume it is an IP or person.
3. Correlate NAS/VPN/WLAN/switch request/retry/session evidence and called station/site. Determine whether ten NPS rows are one retrying exchange or repeated access attempts.
4. Inspect account type, owner, lock/disable/expiry/password-change state, authentication method, EAP/certificate/MFA, connection/network policy, DC selected, and related 6272/6273/6274/6279 events.
5. Compare other accounts/stations/NASs, source IP/device where independently available, geography only as weak context, approved test/change, and service impact.
6. Classify user/device error, cached credential, rollout drift, NAS retry/configuration, directory/NPS fault, authorized test, or suspected guessing/spray. Escalate through identity/network incident procedures.

Never automatically disable/reset/lock an account, revoke sessions/certificates/tokens, block a MAC/IP/NAS, rotate a RADIUS secret, alter policy/EAP/MFA, stop NPS, or isolate a gateway from this result alone. Shared infrastructure and ambiguous identifiers make automatic action hazardous. If containment is approved, preserve evidence and validate access for unaffected users/devices. Recovery requires understood cause, clean source health, expected identity/NAS behavior, and no recurrence across a reviewed interval; silence from disabled auditing is not recovery.

Retain artifacts listed in `evidence` according to local security/privacy/legal policy. The 90-day estimate is advisory. Use exact bounded post-result suppression only; preserve base findings and source health.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot without turning unknowns into success

- **No 6272/6273:** verify NPS role/service, effective Audit Network Policy Server policy, local Event Viewer, Security log retention, input/forwarder queues, index/source/type, event time, and search RBAC.
- **6273 present but fields null:** inspect raw XML, add-on version/placement, XML mode, field case, props/transforms, and truncation. Do not regex localized rendered text as the permanent fix.
- **Reason 16 volume suddenly spikes:** compare password/profile rollout, station/NAS retries, network policy, correct DC/domain, account existence/lock, NPS/DC/DNS/time health, and approved tests before attack attribution.
- **Calling station is shared or `-`:** exclude it from this primary identity and use NAS/session/controller evidence in a separate detector; never substitute NAS address and call it the endpoint.
- **Two-to-four accounts never alert:** intentional. Monitor the unclassified operational bucket; change cardinality only through measured tuning and regression tests.
- **Duplicate count:** compare NPS/source/EventRecordID and `_indextime`, WEF/direct collection, restored logs, checkpoint reset, and overlapping schedules.
- **CIM count differs:** compare tags, action mapping, acceleration lag, field aliases, and source scope. Raw reason-16 events remain authoritative.
- **Accounting disagrees:** align session/request IDs, NPS/proxy/NAS roles, clock, logging selection, SQL/text health, and retry semantics; accounting and Security records answer different questions.
grandmaExplanation: We watch the service that decides many office Wi-Fi and remote-access sign-ins. When one device sends many wrong-password attempts for one account or several accounts, we alert the team—but we first check retries, stale passwords, and network equipment before calling it an attack.
